title: Load-fidelity harness and customer acceptance procedure for Dedicated capacity
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a deterministic, high-fidelity load harness and an associated acceptance protocol that customers can use (or that we run on their behalf) to validate Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees, autoscaling behavior, and fleet controls before go-live. This ticket captures the end-to-end methodology, test scenarios, automation plan, observability gates, and runbook for handoff to SRE and Solutions Engineering.

Why: Current capacity validation relies on synthetic, uniform token streams which miss realistic burst patterns, KV cache warmup effects, and cross-tenant contention. This results in customer surprises during acceptance (unexpected tail latency during short bursts, slow warmup causing underutilization, and autoscaler oscillation). The new harness should mirror production request distributions, support replay of captured customer traffic, and verify rollback/fallback behaviors so we can provide deterministic throughput commitments and clear acceptance criteria to customers.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run three traffic modes: synthetic steady-state, synthetic microburst (sub-minute spikes), and traffic-replay from recorded customer traces

For a reference Dedicated pool (2 x A100 equivalent), harness demonstrates sustained QPS for model-family X at 95th-percentile latency <= target_latency and 99.9th-percentile tail latency below tail_threshold, measured over 30-minute windows

Autoscaler exercise validates scale-up time, warmup hit rate (KV cache), and scale-down hysteresis; documented numbers must be within SLOs: scale-up latency <= 90s, cache warmup to 80% hit rate within 3 minutes

Fleet controls tested: model-fallback on capacity constraint, region-fallback for cross-region redundancy, and circuit-breaker activation under overload; all transitions are observable in Console dashboards and trigger the expected alerts
Customer acceptance checklist produced (runbook + CSV of metrics) and demo run completed with Solutions Engineering on a pilot customer environment
Automated reports generated post-run that include token-level cost projection, latency percentiles, error breakdowns, and profiler traces for identified hotspots
tasks: Design input traffic generator with support for: Poisson + Pareto inter-arrival models, per-request prompt-size distribution, and KV cache warmup hooks
Implement traffic-replay adapter to take anonymized pcap/trace exports (or request logs) and replay with timeline fidelity
Create an autoscaler probe that simulates realistic queuing and measures scale latency and oscillation under policy settings
Integrate harness with Console metrics and tracing (token-level cost, per-route latency, sampling of request traces) and add dashboards for acceptance runs
Build an acceptance report generator that emits CSV + Markdown summary and links to relevant GitHub PRs and dashboards
Author runbook for Solutions Engineering and SRE: pre-checks, run steps, failure modes, and remediation guidance
progress_updates: 2025-11-11: Spike completed for traffic generator library choices. Decided on extending existing prober with a new workload-shaping layer (will reuse parts of ENG-11522 prober).
2025-11-12: Met with Solutions Eng to define replay formats they can provide; agreed on sanitized JSON trace export (timestamp, prompt_len, model, response_tokens, status).

2025-11-14: Implemented prototype of microburst loader — can generate 10s spikes at 5x baseline QPS and measure instantaneous queue length in the runtime. Initial results show a 15% tail latency increase when cache is cold.
2025-11-16: Autoscaler probe instrumented. Observed scale-down oscillation in a naive policy; added 120s scale-down hysteresis and plan to guard with a moving-average-based decision rule.

2025-11-18: Draft acceptance checklist created and shared with PM and SRE for review (link in links field). Next: run a full acceptance pass on a staging Dedicated pool and iterate on dashboard panels.
